title: Tiered On‑Call Orchestration and Customer Status Playbook
author: Samantha R. Kim
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes Redwood Inference’s standard approach for orchestrating multi‑tier on‑call rotations, executing incident response, publishing customer‑facing status updates, and running periodic game days. It combines high‑level process with concrete runbook examples, postmortem expectations, escalation matrices, and ready‑to‑use communication templates. Use this page as the canonical reference for on‑call leads, SREs, and engineering incident responders.

Goals and scope:
- Keep customer impact small and recovery time predictable (SLOs below).
- Surface triage and remediation runbooks for common failure modes.
- Provide templates for status page updates and customer comms.
- Define game day scenarios and success criteria for operational readiness.

Key SLAs and SLOs (platform level):
| Metric | SLO | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| API p95 latency (hosted) | < 250 ms | 300 ms sustained for 5m | eng-platform
| Error rate (5xx) | < 0.5% | 1% sustained for 1m | eng-serving-runtime
| Request loss / failed allocations | < 0.05% | 0.2% any 1m window | eng-sre
| Status page uptime | 99.9% | 5m outage | eng-sre

High‑level incident lifecycle (quick steps):
1) Detection & acknowledgement — automated alert or customer report. Acknowledge within 3 minutes for P0/P1.
2) Triage — determine scope (regional/global), impact (latency, errors, data loss), and initial mitigation.
3) Declare incident level and create incident channel (Slack + PagerDuty if P0/P1).
4) Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead, Tech Lead, Scribe.
5) Remediate — execute runbook, scale/route around failure, apply rollback if needed.
6) Customer updates — publish to status page and email templates every 30–60 minutes while impact persists.
7) Resolution & recovery validation — confirm metrics recovered for 15 minutes.
8) Postmortem — 72‑hour initial blameless report; full RCA within 7 business days for P0/P1.

Incident severity definitions (team common language):
- P0 (Critical): Global service outage or data loss impacting customers. IC required immediately.
- P1 (Major): Significant degradation (large customer subsets, severe latency), partial outages.
- P2 (Moderate): Localized degradation, single feature degradation, mitigations available.
- P3 (Minor): Low user impact, non‑urgent.

Escalation matrix (basic):
1) PagerDuty alert to on‑call engineer (T0). 3 minutes to acknowledge.
2) If unacknowledged, escalate to on‑call manager (T1) automatically. 7 minute total window to IC.
3) If still unresolved at 15m for P0/P1, page engineering director and product lead.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): Triage, priorities, declares severity, coordinates cross‑team work.
- Communications Lead: Manages internal comms, status page, customer emails.
- Tech Lead: Owns technical remediation decisions, rollbacks, and postmortem inputs.
- Scribe: Real‑time notes and timeline.
- Escalation Contacts: Listed in the on‑call roster (private link).

Runbook: High latency, multi‑region (example)
Purpose: recover p95 latency regressions for text generation endpoints.
When to use: p95 > 300 ms sustained for 5 minutes, or >1% 5xx correlated.
Pre‑reqs: access to Grafana, internal tracing, router and model routing dashboard, autoscaler CLI.
Step by step:
1) Confirm scope:
   - Open Grafana panel: API latency by region.
   - Run: curl -s https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/query?query=api_p95
   - Determine whether issue is global or regional; list affected regions.
2) Immediately increase capacity for affected region(s):
   - Run autoscaler command: rwi-autoscale --pool inference-pool-<region> --add 10
   - Confirm nodes provisioned: rwi-nodes list --region <region>
3) If increase fails or latencies remain high, switch routing to a lower‑latency model variant:
   - Update router: rwi-router set-route --route /generate --model redwood-medium-v1 --weight 0.6
   - Verify traffic shift in 60s.
4) Apply prefix caching bypass where hot‑key issues observed:
   - Disable prefix cache for the route: rwi-config set --route /generate --prefix_caching false
   - Monitor cache miss ratio.
5) If 5xx spike accompanies latency, collect heap profiles and GPU metrics and open a debug session with runtime team.
6) When p95 < 250 ms for 15 continuous minutes, mark runbook success and begin rollback of temporary mitigations (weighted routing, autoscale overruns).

Postmortem requirements and template (P0/P1):
- Initial summary within 72 hours (blameless).
- Full postmortem with timeline, impact table, root cause, remediation plan, owners, and verification steps within 7 business days.
- Postmortem must include quantitative impact (requests affected, downtime minutes, customer list) and any regulatory or legal implications.

Postmortem template (copy/paste):
Title:
Severity (P0/P1/P2):
Date/time window:
Incident Commander:
Summary (3–5 sentences):
Impact (customers affected, minutes of degraded service, error counts):
Timeline (ordered, timestamps, role actions):
Root cause (what failed and why):
Contributing factors:
Immediate mitigations applied:
Permanent remediation actions and owners (with deadlines):
Detection & monitoring gaps:
Follow‑ups (changelogs, tests, dashboards to add):
Verification plan (how we will validate fix):
Lessons learned and process changes:

On‑call rotation and coverage model:
- Primary on‑call window: 08:00–20:00 local office hours (regional stagger) — covers most customer traffic.
- Night/weekend on‑call: single engineer with manager backup for P0/P1.
- Rotation length: 2 weeks for engineers; 4 weeks for ops leads.
- Handover checklist (must be completed every shift change):
  1. Confirm there are no active incidents in status.
  2. Review pending alerts and suppressed alerts (PagerDuty).
  3. Run quick health checks: rwi-healthcheck --full.
  4. Share notes in rotation channel and mention incoming outgoing on call Slack thread.

Game day program (quarterly):
Purpose: validate cross‑team incident response, runbooks, and customer comms.
Frequency: quarterly per team; company‑wide once a year.
Sample scenarios:
- Global model routing failure (simulate routing table corruption).
- Rapid cluster eviction (simulate mass preemptions).
- Status page outage while incident is active (exercise fallback comms).
Success criteria:
- IC assigned within 3 minutes, initial public status update within 30 minutes, mitigation executed within 60 minutes for P0 scenario.
- Postgame postmortem and action items published within 7 days.

Status page and customer communication templates
Status page components:
- Short title (one line)
- Summary (2–3 sentences)
- Impact (bullet list of affected features/regions)
- Mitigation (what we are doing now)
- Next update window and timeline
- Root cause & resolution (filled after RCA)

Public status page template (initial):
Title: Service degradation affecting text generation API
Summary: We are currently experiencing elevated latency and errors for text generation in multiple regions. Our team is investigating.
Impact: Customers in eu‑west1 and us‑west1 may see increased response times and occasional errors.
Mitigation: We have increased capacity and are routing traffic to healthy model variants.
Next update: We will post an update within 30 minutes or sooner if the situation changes.

Customer email template (P0 initial):
Subject: Incident: Reductions in text generation availability — [Region list]
Body:
Hello —

We are investigating an issue causing reduced availability and increased latency for the text generation API in [regions]. Our engineering team has declared an incident and is actively working on mitigation steps. We have increased capacity and routed traffic to fallback model variants.

What we’re doing now:
- Capacity increases in impacted regions
- Routing adjustments to fallback model variants
- Ongoing metric and trace collection for root cause analysis

We will update you by [time window] or sooner as we make progress. If you are experiencing data loss or impact to SLAs, please reply to this message and include your account ID so we can prioritize.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Operations

Internal escalation: sample Slack play and commands:
- Create incident channel: /incident create "INC-<short>" --severity P0 --owner @oncall_ic
- Post initial status: /incident post "Investigating elevated latency in eu‑west1"
- Runbooks and dashboards pinned to channel.

Observability and tooling checklist (pre‑shift):
- Grafana dashboards pinned to rotation channel.
- Traces are sampling at 100% for error paths.
- Alert noise filters reviewed weekly; threshold tuning documented.

Auditing and compliance notes:
- All incident actions and customer comms must be archived in the incident folder for 1 year.
- For incidents involving customer data, contact security@redwood with the incident ID within 2 hours.

Appendix: common short runbooks (links)
- Model OOM / GPU eviction: rwi-runbooks/model-oom (runbook link)
- Certificate expiry causing TLS errors: rwi-runbooks/cert-rotation
- Status page fallback when ops status site is down: rwi-runbooks/statuspage-fallback
